# NOTES: "The Layton Court Mystery" by Anthony Berkeley (Gutenberg #72883). Single book, 28 chapters plus dedication/preface. Narrator third person, comic tone.

## Front matter
- Dedication "To my Father". Preface letter: author says detective should behave realistically, make mistakes; evidence presented fairly to reader in order discovered.

## Characters
- **Roger Sheringham**: amateur detective, author, <40 yrs, Winchester & Oxford, stocky, round face, gray eyes, big-bowled pipe, eccentric clothes (grey flannel trousers, old Norfolk jacket). Calls unmarried ladies under 30 by first names. Half-blue in golf. Narrates "Watson/Sherlock" games with Alec.
- **Alexander "Alec" Grierson**: his friend, big broad-shouldered, cheerful, Oxford cricketer (3 yrs for Oxford), Scottish-ish (called "Scotch" by Roger), from Worcestershire boyhood, age ~24-ish implied (Roger says Stanworth's "boy" line refers to Alec age 24). Engaged to Barbara Shannon on day 1 (Alec says "yesterday"), breaks off next morning.
- **Victor Stanworth**: host, ~60, bachelor, City financier, genial, half-crown cigars, pre-war whiskey. Brother's widow is Lady Cynthia (Stanworth). Actually: younger brother married Lady Cynthia Anglemere (eldest daughter of Earl of Grassingham); brother dead ~10 yrs; Stanworth settles £1,000/yr on her. Secret blackmailer; keeps evidence in safe; carries safe around.
- **Lady Stanworth** (Lady Cynthia): tall, stately, graying, cool. Hostess. Hates Stanworth. Secretly married Jefferson ~6 months before; after death she is "Lady Jefferson". Stanworth blackmailed her over her father (Earl) — threat to expose; she married brother Victor's brother? (her blackmail: marry his younger brother or father exposed; she chose the brother).
- **Major Harry Jefferson**: sallow, tall, taciturn, ex-army, Stanworth's secretary/dogsbody (6 years with him). Former officer; forged-check scandal: he confessed for a friend's forged check, lost commission, Stanworth blackmailed him into secretaryship. Plays good tennis. Innocent of murder per later evidence.
- **Graves** (real name Bill Higgins): butler, ex-prize-fighter, ~20 years in service of Stanworth (Major says "twenty years"); Stanworth held over him a hanging threat (murderer in small way); bodyguard role.
- **Mrs. Shannon**: small, fair, doll-like, peevish; mother of Barbara; blackmail target (Stanworth held info about her past).
- **Barbara Shannon**: ~19, small, slight, gray eyes, fair hair, firm chin. Engaged to Alec then broke off. Was in library night of murder; Stanworth blackmailed her (marry Alec within a month or expose mother). Defied him. Shannons leave on 2:41 train with Mrs. Shannon? (Barbara and Mother leave with party "two forty-one" in morning — Mertons' visit next month.)
- **Mrs. Mary Plant**: dark-haired, ~26, husband in Soudanese Civil Service; Stanworth blackmailed her over pre-marriage incident; she paid him; he demanded £250 in 3 months. Took jewels to library (night ~12:30) to hand over; told police false story (jewels locked "day before"). Fainted at news. Perfume "Parfum Jasmine" (9s 6d). Handkerchief left on settee.
- **Inspector Mansfield** of Elchester police: methodical, sharp.
- **Doctor Matthewson**: examined Stanworth earlier for hay fever; healthy.
- **William**: gardener, melancholy, hates Roger; wife (Mrs. William) at lodge, cook's "brother" John Prince visited.
- **John Prince** ("Prince John"): big farm hand at Hillcrest Farm (Mr. Wetherby's); went for Stanworth earlier in broad daylight; dangerous; red herring. Won prize at Elchester Agricultural Show; back late.
- **Chapman**: chauffeur; car kept ready.
- **Alice** and **Mary** (maids). Mary tidied library night before; settee brushed; no pen found.
- **Rudgeman**: constable.
- Landlord (unnamed, "Albert" reference), ancient rustic, porter.

## Setting
- Layton Court, Hertfordshire, Jacobean; library: oak panelling, fireplace blocked, French windows (to lawn), sash window (rose garden side) with anti-burglar fitting, small lattice window in corner, door to hall. Safe by wall near typewriter table. Settee (black, angle between sash window and fireplace). Writing table central. Dining room adjacent; gunroom/storeroom between library and dining room; drawing room and morning room front of house. Ash pit behind house. Lodge gates. Village ~1.5 miles; Elchester 10 miles bike.

## Timeline
- **Day 1 morning, ~8am**: Roger in rose garden with William (greenfly). Alec arrives, has been to village to "post a letter" (actually to bookmaker). Barbara tells Alec she can't marry him ("something dreadful happened").
- **8:30–10**: Breakfast; Jefferson called out by Graves. Lady Stanworth tells Roger & Alec library doors locked; they break door; Jefferson: "Mr. Stanworth appears to have shot himself."
- Body: slumped in chair behind writing table, revolver in right hand, wound in centre forehead, edges blackened. Typed confession "For reasons that concern only myself, I have decided to kill myself," signed Victor Stanworth; earlier attempt "V-i-c" above.
- Roger opens windows; Graves finds paper; Jefferson searches dead man's pockets; Roger notes bruise? (scratch on right wrist).
- Mrs. Plant caught at safe, claims jewels; Roger covers for her.
- Inspector Mansfield arrives; Dr. Matthewson: died ~2am; bullet extracted from scalp; one shell fired; revolver not fully loaded.
- Jefferson reluctant to open safe; keys found in upper waistcoat pocket (wrong pocket); safe opened ~noon: share certificates, cash-box ~£4,000+, Mrs. Plant's jewel-box (green leather). Lady Stanworth identifies jewels.
- Roger notices vase missing (pair on chimney-piece; one blue vase). Broken vase fragments; bullet hole in panelling behind pillar on left of chimney-piece (bullet dug out with penknife). Second shot fired.
- Roger's hypotheses: murder. Shell extracted; confession forged (typed, found in waste-paper basket: signature sheet; fountain pen flooded).
- Roger finds blotter marks; second sheet in basket.
- Footprint outside lattice window (large boot, ~size 10/11, stepped backward); second footprint; footprints later smoothed (Alec did it). Roger deduces lattice window handle trick.
- Ash pit: scrap of pencil letter "…that brute Prince… this neighbourhood… serious danger… fright of my life this morning…"
- Roger chases Prince; visits lodge (Mrs. William: Prince dangerous, attacked Stanworth earlier); pub landlord; Hillcrest Farm; bull chase (Alec & Roger run; ancient rustic laughs).
- Station: no stranger.
- William: a large strange man at lodge ~8:30 pm, "cook's brother."
- Blue vase fragments found in laurel shrubbery.
- Settee: handkerchief (jasmine scent) and fair hair, powder smudge on arm.
- Maid Mary: library tidied night before; settee brushed; no pen.
- Dinner: Lady Stanworth says she visited drawing, morning room, upstairs; Mrs. Plant claims only drawing room.
- Night: Roger & Alec search morning room papers; find five passbooks, three in other names; large cash payments; Roger guesses blackmail.
- Next morning: inquest at morning room 11 am; verdict "Suicide during temporary insanity."
- Roger questions Mrs. Plant in rose garden; she confesses blackmail, that she visited library 12:30; Stanworth demanded £250 in 3 months; she says Jefferson did NOT come in; she received typed letter from Stanworth (posted from village by 8:30 post) saying he'd burned evidence and would kill himself.
- Roger confronts Jefferson; Jefferson reveals his forged-check story and that he married Lady Stanworth secretly 6 months ago; alibi: with wife.
- Lady Stanworth statement—Roger's theory collapses.
- Train back to London; Roger reveals Alec killed Stanworth. Alec's account: couldn't sleep; went to library ~ night; hid behind curtain; saw Mrs. Plant (crying); Stanworth blackmail; then Barbara came, Stanworth blackmailed her (marry Alec within a month or expose Mrs. Shannon). Barbara defied him and broke off engagement. Alec confronted Stanworth; Stanworth fired, missed (hit vase); Alec twisted wrist and shot him. Alec removed first shell, burned ~16-17 blackmail envelopes in hearth, typed letters to Mrs. Plant, Jefferson, Lady Stanworth (Barbara's?), typed confession. Escaped via lattice window; handle trick; footprints; returned via dining room windows.
- Roger: don't tell Barbara. Alec asks whether to tell police; Roger rejects conventional idea.

## Key objects/clues
- Chimney-piece ring marks; pair of blue vases; bullet in panel.
- Blotter scratch marks; fountain pen flood; confession typed on sheet from waste basket.
- Safe combination via makers; keys in wrong waistcoat pocket.
- Lattice window handle trick; footprints (heel deeper) outside sash/lattice.
- Ash pit pencil note "that brute Prince".
- Handkerchief (jasmine), fair hair (Barbara's), face powder.
- Stanworth's wrist scratch.

## Final
Ending line: Roger: "For heaven's sake, Alec, _do_ try sometimes not to be so disgustingly conventional!"
